correctness.rationale: For the specified directed model, conditioned on the iid colors, non-root adjacency rows and root outgoing edges yield iid trivalent contributions. A moderate-deviation local theorem for a difference of two binomials controls probabilities of equal and one-off color degrees with relative error O(log(n)^2/sqrt(n)); the conditional mean is negligible relative to variance, giving a 1/2 sign limit when many eligible vertices exist and a probability-1 outcome when none exists. A Gaussian global color imbalance gives the critical crossover; Bernstein handles vanishing missing-edge intensity. Self-loop impact is O(n^-1/2). The bundled finite exhaustive checker verifies the exact reduction up to four vertices and conditional row laws up to eleven, not the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: A natural formula explicitly highlighted in the motivating 2026 paper as nonconvergent on complete regular trees undergoes a sharp, nontrivial normal crossover when random graph edges are almost all present. The exact 1/log(n) width is derived from a structural balance between n candidate successors and a conditioned moderate-deviation factor, giving a complete probability phase diagram in the near-complete regime. This is a mathematically motivated boundary, not a minor finite count.
